articles.title: 'Amor não termina com a despedida', diz filho de Ayres Rocha | G1
articles.standfirst: Álvaro Neto publicou homenagem ao pai em suas redes sociais. Ayres morreu na quarta (14), em decorrência de um câncer. Ele foi apresentador da Rede Amazônica por mais de 30 anos.
articles.summary: Álvaro Neto publicou homenagem ao pai em suas redes sociais. Ayres morreu na quarta (14), em decorrência de um câncer. Ele foi apresentador da Rede Amazônica por mais de 30 anos.
articles.body:
Para Álvaro, o relato é uma forma de eternizar um momento importante: a despedida de seu pai, Ayres Rocha — Foto: Arquivo/Instagram

🖤🥀 "Percebemos que o amor não termina com a despedida . Ele permanece em nós, nas marcas que essa pessoa deixou, nos valores que nos ensinou e em cada lembrança que o tempo jamais poderá apagar".

O advogado Álvaro Neto, filho do jornalista e apresentador Ayres Rocha, publicou uma homenagem nas redes sociais sobre a morte do pai. Um dos nomes mais conhecidos da comunicação acreana, Ayres morreu na quarta-feira (14) após complicações de um câncer .

Em sua publicação, Álvaro conta sobre a dificuldade em compartilhar um momento difícil como este. Para ele, o relato é uma forma de eternizar momentos importantes com o pai.

Segundo o advogado, o último abraço dos dois foi no dia 12 de setembro deste ano. Mesmo com a dificuldade de colocar em palavras o que sente, Álvaro conta da luta e o que pôde fazer, tanto na parte profissional quanto na emocional, para ajudar o pai a enfrentar a doença e tentar mudar essa história.

“Lutei com tudo o que pude, mas hoje preciso aceitar que existem coisas que fogem às nossas mãos. A morte me assusta, não porque é o fim, e sim porque ela vem e leva pessoas especiais que marcaram nossas vidas com alegria, amor, sorrisos e abraços. E, em meio a tanta dor, carrego uma gratidão imensa nesse avião por ele tentar me esperar chegar para que pudéssemos nos despedir”, continuou.

O advogado lembra ainda que, até o último momento, Ayres demonstrou consideração, amor e cuidado com ele e com a família. Além disso, agradeceu por todos os ensinamentos que aprendeu com o pai.

“Ficará para sempre guardado no meu coração. Obrigado por tudo o que você foi e por tudo o que fez por mim. Obrigado pelo cuidado, pelo amor, pela presença, pelo silêncio e, principalmente, pelos valores que me ensinou. Se hoje sou quem sou, existe muito de você em mim. Sua integridade, seu caráter e a pessoa maravilhosa que você foi e se tornou, continuarão vivos naquilo que deixou em nós”, afirmou.

A publicação continua com a constatação de que o apresentador era querido e admirado por muitas pessoas, e que deixou um legado no jornalismo acreano.

“Hoje ficam a saudade, as lembranças e tudo aquilo que o tempo jamais poderá apagar. Não vou fingir que entendo os desígnios de Deus. Há dores que simplesmente não conseguimos explicar. Mas continuo confiando nele. [...] A minha fé não me impede de sentir essa dor. Ela me sustenta enquanto a atravesso. Me despeço do meu pai com o coração partido, mas profundamente grato por ter tido o privilégio de ser seu filho”, finalizou a homenagem.

Álvaro relembrou os momentos de alegria junto a Ayres — Foto: Arquivo/Instagram

Nessa quinta-feira (15), após o sepultamento do pai , Álvaro publicou mais um texto sobre esse momento difícil.

"O peso de carregar um caixão não está apenas naquilo que os braços suportam, mas em tudo aquilo que o coração carrega. Ali estão as lembranças, os abraços que não se repetirão, as conversas que deixarão saudade, os ensinamentos que permanecerão e uma história inteira compartilhada com alguém que amamos. Naquele momento, cada passo parece carregar uma vida inteira de memórias. O corpo sente o peso, mas é a alma que tenta compreender a ausência", destacou.

José Ayres de Souza Rocha nasceu e cresceu em Rio Branco . Caçula de uma família com nove filhos biológicos e duas filhas adotivas, ele começou a trabalhar na televisão em 1989, quase por acaso.

Na época, trabalhava como bancário durante a manhã e procurava uma segunda ocupação para preencher as tardes. Foi assim que surgiu a oportunidade na então TV Acre.

No início, passou meses observando o trabalho dos profissionais da redação até receber um convite inesperado para substituir o apresentador de um programa esportivo que havia faltado. Mesmo receoso de encarar as câmeras, aceitou o desafio.

Ayres Rocha se despediu da bancada do JAC2 em 8 de novembro de 2024, após mais de 30 anos à frente do telejornal — Foto: Rede Amazônica

A experiência abriu caminho para uma carreira que acompanharia as transformações do telejornalismo acreano.

Ayres passou por diferentes telejornais da emissora, nas edições da manhã e da tarde, até assumir a bancada do JAC2, que estreou em 1995. Ao longo dos anos, também buscou formação acadêmica na área de Comunicação Social e ficou conhecido entre os colegas pelo apelido de “professor”.

Em 2019, o jornalista representou o Acre na edição comemorativa dos 50 anos do Jornal Nacional , em uma participação que marcou sua carreira e levou o sotaque acreano ao principal telejornal do país.

Em 2022, participou de uma campanha do Novembro Azul da Rede Amazônica Acre, na qual contou que havia recebido o diagnóstico de câncer de próstata aos 50 anos e incentivou outros homens a procurar atendimento médico.

Na despedida do JAC2, em 2024, o jornalista encerrou a apresentação com a mesma naturalidade que marcou sua passagem pela bancada . Ao final, veio a frase que tantas pessoas ouviram durante anos, na voz inconfundível do apresentador:

“Jornal do Acre 2ª edição fica por aqui. Para você, uma ótima noite, e a gente se vê por aí''.

articles.title: UBS na região de Itapetininga realizam ações de Outubro Rosa | G1
articles.standfirst: Entre as ações estão a coleta de papanicolau, exames de mamografia e até palestras médicas. Na região de Itapetininga, os atendimentos começam neste sábado (17) e seguem até o fim do mês.
articles.summary: Na região de Itapetininga (SP), as Unidades Básicas de Saúde (UBS) promovem uma série de ações ligadas ao Outubro Rosa.
articles.body:
O Outubro Rosa reforça a importância da prevenção, do acompanhamento médico e da detecção precoce do câncer de mama — Foto: Reprodução/Magnific

Outubro é marcado pelas campanhas de conscientização sobre a prevenção e o diagnóstico precoce dos cânceres de mama e do colo do útero. Na região de Itapetininga (SP), as Unidades Básicas de Saúde (UBSs) promovem uma série de ações voltadas à saúde da mulher.

A programação inclui mamografias, coleta de exames de Papanicolau, testes rápidos, solicitação de exames e palestras com profissionais de saúde sobre a importância da prevenção.

As atividades começam nesta sexta-feira (16), também serão realizadas no sábado (17) e seguem até o fim do mês. Para participar, é necessário apresentar um documento de identificação com foto, como RG, ou CPF, além do Cartão Nacional de Saúde (Cartão SUS).

Realização do exame de mamografia — Foto: HCAA

As moradoras de Manduri (SP) podem participar das ações voltadas à Campanha de Outubro Rosa, com o objetivo de conscientizar sobre a importância da prevenção e do diagnóstico precoce do câncer de mama e do colo do útero.

Nas unidades básicas de saúde, as mulheres podem fazer o exame preventivo de Papanicolau e solicitar a mamografia, somente para mulheres com idade acima de 50 anos.

UBS 'Maria Inêz Melício', em Manduri (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/Google Street View

Na cidade, as ações começam às 16h e seguem até às 20h desta sexta-feira (16), na UBS Maria Inêz Melício.

As atividades seguem na segunda-feira (19), das 16h às 20h, na UBS Doutor Aldemar Holtz de Almeida;

No sábado (24), acontece o Dia D, das 8h às 17h, nas unidades Maria Inêz Melício e Aldemar Holtz de Almeida;

Na quarta-feira (28), o atendimento é feito das 16h às 20h, também na UBS Maria Inêz Melício;

Já na quinta-feira (29), as ações acontecem das 16h às 20h, no posto de saúde Olívio Nicoletti, na Vila São Berto.

Em Angatuba, as ações começam às 08h e seguem até às 11h neste sábado, na Casa Rosa, localizada na Rua Major Pereira de Morais, 656, na região central. Lá, a coleta do Papanicolau acontece por demanda.

De acordo com a prefeitura, a coleta do exame de Papanicolau facilita o acesso das mulheres à prevenção. As coletas seguem em horário estendido, das 16h às 18h, nas unidades de Estratégia Saúde da Família (ESF) da cidade, nos seguintes dias:

A prefeitura promove as ações de prevenção e cuidado com a saúde da mulher através da coleta de exame Papanicolau, das 9h às 17h deste sábado (17). O atendimento é voltado para mulheres de 25 a 64 anos.

As ações ocorrem no Posto Adonai, localizado na Rua Persides Pires do Amaral, 55. Lá, o atendimento será realizado mediante agendamento prévio, na recepção do posto apresentando o Cartão Família.

O Posto Adonai fica localizado na Rua Persides Pires do Amaral, em Porangaba — Foto: Google Street View/Reprodução

Na cidade, a campanha do outubro rosa é realizada na ESF Urbano e Chácara das Flores, neste sábado (17), das 08h às 15h. Segundo a prefeitura, o objetivo é conscientizar sobre a prevenção e o diagnóstico precoce do câncer de mama e do colo de útero.

Nas duas unidades, as mulheres podem participar de palestras com uma equipe de psicologia, emissão de guia para mamografia e a coleta de Papanicolau.

Conforme a Prefeitura de Timburi, as ações de prevenção e cuidados com a população acontecem neste sábado (17), das 8h às 16h, no Centro de Saúde de Timburi.

Na unidade, as mulheres podem realizar exame de Papanicolau, avaliação da pré-diabetes, atualizar a carteira de vacinação e os beneficiários do Bolsa Família podem fazer a pesagem.

Espéculo vaginal é usado em exames como o papanicolau ou exame de HPV — Foto: Adobe Stock

Em Itaberá, as mulheres podem participar das ações a partir das 07h30 até às 16h, neste sábado (17). Os exames preventivos e o ultrassom da mama são realizados na Unidade de Saúde da Mulher, ao lado do hospital da cidade.

Segundo a prefeitura, as ações de cuidados com a saúde da mulher, que fazem parte da campanha do Outubro Rosa, acontecem neste sábado (17) nas unidades Central, do CDHU e Estação, das 8h às 15h.

Nas unidades, as mulheres podem fazer a coleta do exame preventivo de Papanicolau, solicitar a mamografia, passar por consultas com a enfermagem em saúde da mulher e receber orientações sobre prevenção e cuidados com a saúde.

A Prefeitura de Campina do Monte Alegre informou que, na cidade, as atividades relacionadas ao Outubro Rosa começam na segunda-feira (19) e seguem até quinta-feira (22), das 17h30 às 20h30, na UBS Serginho, localizada na Rua Roberto Ivens Vieira, 316.

Nas datas, as moradoras da cidade podem realizar a coleta do exame de Papanicolau. As ações se encerram na quinta-feira (23), a partir das 18h, com palestra médica e até o sorteio de brindes.

A UBS Serginho em Campina do Monte Alegre fica localizada na Rua Roberto Ivens Vieira, 316 — Foto: Google Maps/Reprodução

No sábado (24), a Prefeitura de Bernardino de Campos realiza uma ação especial, com atendimento em todas as Unidades de Saúde da cidade. O atendimento acontece das 8h às 15h e não há a necessidade de um agendamento prévio.

Durante as ações, serão realizados exames preventivos para mulheres de 24 a 64 anos. Além disso, as mulheres acima de 40 anos poderão solicitar a mamografia.

De terça-feira (20) a quarta-feira (21), as moradoras de Conchas (SP) podem passar por exame de Papanicolau, auto exame de mamografia e os grupos de risco de câncer podem solicitar exames.

Nos dias, as unidades da Praça, do Bosque e da Cohab funcionam em horário estendido, sendo das 16h às 20h. É necessário que as moradoras levem um documento com foto, cartão do SUS e da unidade de saúde da família.

articles.title: In 2020, members of a Michigan farming family signed solar-option agreements covering 562.8 acres; a judge has now ruled them valid, keeping nearly 30% of a proposed $330 million solar project in play
articles.summary: A legal battle over farmland in western Michigan has ended with a ruling that could keep a major solar development moving.
articles.body: A legal battle over farmland in western Michigan has ended with a ruling that could keep a major solar development moving. For the Smallegan family, however, the decision means hundreds of acres tied to their agricultural land will remain under agreements with renewable energy developer RWE, bringing a long-running dispute over the future of the property into sharper focus, states an online report by Fox17.Judge upholds solar agreementsAccording to the report, Ottawa County Circuit Judge Jon Hulsing has ruled in favour of RWE Solar Development, finding that the company properly exercised lease options covering about 562.8 acres owned by members of the Smallegan family.The land forms a significant part of the proposed Silver Maple Solar project, a roughly 1,900-acre development planned across Zeeland and Jamestown townships. The family’s property accounts for almost 30% of the proposed project footprint, making the agreements central to the development's viability, states the online report. The dispute stemmed from contracts signed in November 2020. Under the agreements, RWE had five years to study the properties and exercise options to lease the land for solar development, the report adds.The dispute over a five-year windowThe family argued that the agreements were understood to provide a limited period for studying the land rather than establishing a longer-term commitment to solar development. The court rejected that interpretation, finding that the contracts clearly allowed RWE to exercise the options during the five-year period. The judge also dismissed claims that the agreements were obtained under duress, were unfair or were otherwise invalid.Much of the trial focused on whether RWE had properly exercised its options before the November 19, 2025 deadline, clears the Fox17 report.A question of deliveryRWE said the required notices were prepared at its Austin, Texas, office and sent by FedEx on November 13, 2025. Members of the Smallegan family maintained that they never received them.The court found that the agreements considered delivery complete three days after the notices were deposited with an overnight courier. That placed the effective delivery date on November 16, three days before the deadline.The ruling also pointed to subsequent activity involving the property, including more than $282,000 in post-option payments accepted by Patricia Smallegan and communications concerning ownership transfers, as evidence supporting RWE's position that the notices had reached the family.What the ruling means for the landWith the options deemed valid, RWE now holds exclusive possessory rights to the disputed acreage under the agreements. The ruling prevents the family from interfering with the company's rights and requires them to withdraw permissions for activities such as farming and hunting on the affected land.The decision also allows RWE to remove crops and take other steps consistent with its contractual rights. In a particularly consequential part of the order, the family is restricted from participating in administrative, legislative or judicial proceedings opposing the project while the agreements remain in force, based on cooperation provisions contained in the contracts.Solar project still faces hurdlesThe ruling does not mean construction can begin immediately. Silver Maple Solar still requires approval from the Michigan Public Service Commission, leaving another regulatory stage ahead. The Smallegan family is also considering an appeal, meaning the legal dispute may not yet be over, adds the report by Fox17.If the project ultimately receives the necessary approvals, the court decision removes a major obstacle by preserving access to nearly 30% of the planned site. For now, the case highlights the growing tension surrounding the conversion of agricultural land for renewable energy projects, where long-term energy ambitions increasingly intersect with questions about land ownership, farming and the future use of rural communities.Images Courtesy: istockYou use AI every day. articles.title: 'Once again, an abduction': Aides claim Neha Bora taken to unknown location by police
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Aides of All India Students' Association (AISA) chief Neha Bora on Friday claimed that she had been taken to an unknown location after being
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Aides of All India Students' Association (AISA) chief Neha Bora on Friday claimed that she had been taken to an unknown location after being detained by Delhi Police while on her way to participate in the ''Lehra Do Tiranga' protest in the national capital."Neha Bora detained alone, taken to unknown location," a post on her X account read adding that she did not have her phone with her."Delhi Police must answer: where is Neha?" the message said, describing the incident as “once again, an abduction”.Bora was detained at Mandi House, a short while after Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Abhijeet Dipke was picked up from his residence in Jhandewalan, as both headed to participate in the proposed protest on Friday.The detentions triggered jostling among protesters, camera crews and security personnel amid heightened security arrangements across the capital.Police sources told news agency PTI that Dipke was taken to Jafarpur Kalan police station after being detained. The location where Bora was taken was not immediately clear from the information available.Also Read: SIR protests: Opposition has found common ground. But can it stay united?Earlier in the day, more than 20 Delhi Police personnel visited Dipke’s residence in Jhandewalan and served him a notice directing him to refrain from any action that could prejudice the rights of citizens, traders, commuters, patients and others.A senior police officer confirmed the detention of both leaders, saying the situation remained peaceful.“We have detained Dipke and Bora. The situation is very peaceful. Some protesters have reached Connaught Place and will be removed soon. Our main objective is to maintain law and order and ensure smooth traffic movement,” the officer said.Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar visited the DCP New Delhi office at Parliament Street police station to review security arrangements.Security personnel cordoned off Central Park in Connaught Place, forming a human chain along its metal railings. A tear gas vehicle and a Vajra vehicle were stationed outside the park, while Rapid Action Force personnel were deployed inside. Traffic police personnel were also deployed to regulate movement along Connaught Place's inner and outer circles.Hundreds of protesters, including members of CJP and student organisations, gathered at Connaught Place and Mandi House for a series of flash protests, waving the national flag amid heavy police deployment.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Russian officer helped Ukraine kill over 300 troops by leaking military secrets: Report
articles.summary: A Russian army lieutenant secretly supplied Ukraine with troop positions, military plans and other sensitive information, helping Kyiv kill more than 300
articles.body: A Russian army lieutenant secretly supplied Ukraine with troop positions, military plans and other sensitive information, helping Kyiv kill more than 300 Russian soldiers.Lev Stupnikov, who served as chief signals officer in Russia’s 36th Motor Rifle Brigade, used his access to military communications and operational details to help Ukrainian forces identify targets and launch deadly strikes against his own unit.Stupnikov’s first major operation came in February 2024, when Russian soldiers and senior officers gathered for a training exercise near the front line in eastern Ukraine.He photographed the troops, estimated their numbers and sent the exact coordinates of the field to his Ukrainian handler. After being warned to leave the area, he moved away as Ukrainian forces launched a barrage of missiles.His phone buzzed. “Were there explosions? Send a photo.”“There’s just meat,” he answered, according to Wall Street Journal.Stupnikov later counted and informed Ukraine handlers that 68 Russian soldiers had been killed and 60 wounded. Ten of the dead were officers, including Colonel Gusein Musayev, commander of the 36th Motor Rifle Brigade.The strike marked the beginning of a series of attacks aided by Stupnikov’s intelligence. His position as the battalion’s chief signals officer gave him access to troop movements, commanders’ communications, surveillance feeds and battle plans.He passed on radio frequencies, locations of Russian units and details of planned operations, helping Ukrainian forces work out where troops were deployed and when they intended to advance.Stupnikov sabotaged military equipmentHe also undermined his brigade from within. He disabled cameras monitoring Ukrainian territory and tampered with a battery pack connected to a drone controller, causing it to overheat and malfunction during a mission.His information helped Ukraine launch further attacks. In March 2024, Ukrainian forces killed several Russian officers at a brigade gathering identified by Stupnikov. In May, they struck the basement of a former hotel where two Russian assault units were staying, killing 20 soldiers, including a captain. Other intelligence led to an attack on a brigade command post during a meeting of senior officers.The repeated losses raised suspicions among Russian commanders. Stupnikov’s own commander complained that operations were failing and wondered whether a spy had infiltrated the ranks.Stupnikov feared he would soon be exposed after the danger became clear as he accidentally sent his Ukrainian contact a map screenshot showing the location of his own basement. A subsequent strike hit the building, but he survived.His escape across the front lineIn July 2024, Stupnikov received instructions from his Ukrainian contacts to leave his weapons behind and reach an agreed location near the village of Mykilske.Guided by a Ukrainian drone, he crossed no-man’s-land, navigating destroyed vehicles, craters and suspected mines. Ukrainian troops tracked his progress through thermal camera footage and waited for him on the other side.When challenged for the agreed password, he replied, “Peanut shop.”He was searched, blindfolded and taken to safety. Before leaving, he handed Ukrainian forces a smartphone containing access codes to several communication channels, allowing them to continue accessing live feeds from Russian drones and surveillance cameras.Stupnikov later joined the Russian Volunteer Corps, a Ukrainian army unit made up of Russians opposed to Vladimir Putin’s rule. He is now fighting against the Russian forces he once served.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A Pennsylvania woman lived on a 60-acre family farm for 22 years, then agreed to sell it for $250,000 with a proposed 99-year lease letting her stay; an appeals court kept the sale blocked after her siblings objected
articles.summary: A Pennsylvania appeals court has upheld an order blocking the sale of a 60-acre family farm.
articles.body: A Pennsylvania appeals court has upheld an order blocking the sale of a 60-acre family farm. The ruling stops a deal that would have allowed one sister living on the property to sell the land for $250,000 while continuing to live there under a 99-year lease. The Pennsylvania Superior Court upheld an injunction issued by a lower court at the request of the property's co-owners. The legal dispute shows how informal living arrangements involving family property can fall apart when one relative tries to sell the land without the agreement of other heirs. The case involves a rural 60-acre property in western Pennsylvania that has been in the family for generations. According to court records, one sister had lived in a house on the property for 22 years without interruption. She maintained the residential area and treated the farm as her long-term home.The proposed property transactionTensions grew when the sister living on the property reached an agreement to sell the entire 60-acre farm to an outside buyer for $250,000. Under the proposed deal, the buyer also agreed to give her a 99-year lease at a nominal rent. This would allow her to continue living on the land for the rest of her life while receiving money from the sale of the property. After learning about the planned sale, her siblings filed an emergency petition in the local Court of Common Pleas. They asked the court to issue an injunction to stop the transaction. They argued that the farm had been passed down through the family and that the resident sister owned only an undivided share of the property. They said she did not have the legal authority to transfer full ownership of the entire farm to an outside buyer on her own. The trial court granted a preliminary injunction. It barred the sister and the potential buyer from completing the sale or changing the property title until the court could fully review the ownership rights and claims to divide the property.Appeal and legal findingsThe sister living on the farm appealed the injunction to the Superior Court of Pennsylvania under docket number 369 WDA 2026. She argued that her 22 years of living on the property and her continued maintenance of the land gave her the legal and financial grounds to arrange the sale. She also argued that fairness-based legal principles should prevent her co-owners from blocking the agreement. After reviewing the appeal, the Superior Court rejected her arguments and kept the injunction in place. The judges confirmed that under established Pennsylvania property law, people who own property as tenants in common each hold an undivided share of the entire property. This means that one co-owner cannot sign a sales contract that claims to transfer full ownership of the entire property, free of other ownership interests, without the agreement or participation of all the other co-owners. The court also found that allowing the sale to proceed with a 99-year lease would cause serious harm to the other siblings. Such a long-term lease could greatly reduce the property's value, create uncertainty over its legal title, and make any future court-ordered division of the property more difficult. The appeals court stressed that living on a property for many years does not automatically give a co-owner the right to sell the real estate alone or place long-term lease obligations on family land without proper legal authority or a court-ordered division of the property.Next legal proceedingsWith the appeals court keeping the sale blocked, the dispute will return to the trial court. The co-owners are expected to seek a formal partition, a legal process under Pennsylvania law in which jointly owned property is either physically divided among its owners or ordered to be sold through a public or private sale supervised by the court. The proceeds are then distributed according to each heir's legally documented share. Until the court proceedings are completed or the siblings reach an agreement, the injunction will remain in effect. This prevents the sale of the 60-acre family farm and blocks the proposed 99-year residential lease.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Steady improvement in condition': Vatican releases first pictures of Pope Leo XIV after lung surgery
articles.summary: The Vatican on Friday released the first image of Pope Leo XIV since his lung surgery, showing the pontiff attending Mass at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital as
articles.body: The Vatican on Friday released the first image of Pope Leo XIV since his lung surgery, showing the pontiff attending Mass at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital as doctors reported steady progress in his recovery.According to the Holy See Press Office, Pope Leo celebrated Mass in a room prepared on the hospital’s 10th floor, where he is recovering from surgery performed on Tuesday.During his homily, the Pope thanked the hospital staff for their care and dedication. “In his homily, the Pope thanked all the staff—doctors, nurses, and orderlies—for the work they do every day caring for patients in their frailty, and especially for what they have done and continue to do for him,” Vatican News quoted the press office as saying.In a separate health update, the Holy See Press Office announced that new blood tests and a chest X-ray confirmed a steady improvement in Pope Leo XIV’s overall condition.“On his fourth day in hospital, Pope Leo XIV’s doctors say new blood tests and a chest X-ray confirm ‘the steady improvement in his overall condition’,” the statement read.The Vatican added that the pontiff continues to undergo respiratory physiotherapy and is carrying out his daily activities independently as he recovers.Pope Leo XIV, 71, the first US-born pontiff, was admitted to Rome’s Gemelli Hospital on Tuesday for surgery to remove the lower lobe of his right lung after doctors detected a mass. An analysis of tissue collected during the operation confirmed lung adenocarcinoma, a form of lung cancer.The video-assisted procedure lasted approximately 90 minutes. The Vatican said the surgery was completed without complications and that the Pope regained consciousness normally.Earlier medical updates reported reassuring results from routine postoperative checks, with his recovery progressing as expected.Born Robert Prevost in Chicago in 1955, Pope Leo XIV was elected head of the Catholic Church in May 2025. His public engagements have been suspended during his hospitalisation, with the Vatican previously indicating that he was expected to remain in hospital for about a week.(With ANI inputs)You use AI every day. articles.title: 'While with Nitish, I got 9 people murdered': Anant Singh's shocking claim, then clarification
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Bihar MLA Anant Singh made a shocking claim that he had got “nine people murdered” while supporting Nitish Kumar.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Bihar MLA Anant Singh made a shocking claim that he had got “nine people murdered” while supporting Nitish Kumar. The JD(U) leader Singh made the remark during an interview with news agency IANS while describing his long association with the party supremo.Recalling his sacrifices for Nitish Kumar, Mokama MLA claimed: “Who has made as many sacrifices as I have? Nitish Kumar was nothing back then. He used to roam around here and there. At that time, while being with Nitish Kumar, I got nine people murdered,” Singh said.However, later the leader clarified that his remarks was misinterpreted and that he was referring to the killing of nine of his associates, not claiming that he had arranged their murders.Singh said the nine people killed was his personal loss that he suffered after aligning himself with Nitish Kumar and abandoning Lalu Yadav. Singh also claimed that he was shot at during that period. He also recalled that his father died after suffering a heart attack.According to Singh, the killings took place just days after a meeting with Nitish Kumar. He said that although Lalu Prasad Yadav had advised him against attending the meeting, he went ahead and had Nitish Kumar weighed against silver coins.Singh maintained that he had cited these incidents to explain the sacrifices he made while supporting Nitish Kumar. He said his remarks had been taken out of context and denied claiming that he had arranged the murders.Remarks amid dispute over MLC candidateThe controversy comes amid tensions within the Janata Dal (United) over its choice of Neeraj Kumar as the party's candidate for the Patna Graduates' constituency MLC election.Singh has criticised the decision, alleging that Neeraj Kumar had previously opposed him and questioning his contributions to the party. He has insisted that his disagreement is with the candidate selection and not with Nitish Kumar himself.In the same interview, Singh said, “I am a devotee of Nitish. I am not challenging anyone.”Singh also recounted how Nitish Kumar had helped secure an assembly election ticket for his brother by speaking to Lalu Prasad Yadav, who was then allied with Nitish. Singh said he continued to support Nitish after the two leaders parted ways and eventually left Lalu Prasad's camp to join forces with Nitish.Known locally as 'Chhote Sarkar', Singh has continued to oppose Neeraj Kumar's candidature despite reported efforts by senior JD(U) leaders to resolve the disagreement.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: US midterms 2026: DOJ sues California, claims 20,000 suspected ‘noncitizen voters’; seeks to block mail ballots
articles.summary: The US Justice Department has launched a lawsuit against California, claiming over 20,000 noncitizens are registered to vote, as it seeks to halt the counting of mail-in ballots pending citizenship verification ahead of the crucial November 3 elections.
articles.body: The US Justice Department has sued California over allegations that more than 20,000 people suspected of being noncitizens are registered to vote, seeking a court order to prevent their mail-in ballots from being counted in the November 3 midterm elections until their citizenship status is verified.The lawsuit, filed on Thursday, accuses the state of failing to review a list of names provided by federal authorities who believe the individuals may be ineligible to vote in federal elections. The administration is asking a federal judge to require California to set aside ballots from those identified and verify their citizenship before counting them.The case is part of President Donald Trump’s broader push to increase federal oversight of elections ahead of the midterms, in which Republicans face a competitive fight to retain control of both chambers of Congress.According to the Justice Department, Homeland Security Investigations and other federal agencies examined publicly available voter registration records alongside immigration data to identify people considered likely to be noncitizens. The department said the review remains ongoing and described the findings as preliminary.The federal government said it had sent California officials a list of more than 20,000 people it believes are noncitizens who were sent mail-in ballots. It asked state officials to review the names and work with federal agencies to establish whether any were US citizens. The lawsuit alleges that California did not carry out the requested review.Attorney General Todd Blanche said the allegations raised concerns about election integrity and public confidence in the voting system.“State-facilitated voter fraud is unacceptable in the United States of America,” Blanche said. He added that if the state were found responsible in court, it would have undermined confidence in elections and violated laws protecting the country’s system of representative government.First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli said California had been allowed to remove noncitizens from voter rolls and set aside ballots returned by people suspected of being ineligible, but had declined to do so.The lawsuit asks the court to require California to verify the citizenship of the individuals identified by federal authorities, either independently or in cooperation with federal agencies, before counting their mail ballots. It also seeks to prevent the state from tabulating those ballots until the checks are complete.DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said federal agencies had compared voter registration records with immigration data to identify potential noncitizen registrants. He said the analysis was preliminary and that further review was continuing.Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter said the complaint alleges that California was allowing noncitizens to vote in federal elections.You use AI every day. articles.title: Ilhan Omar's husband breaks silence after FBI raid on home; denies concerns over immigration probe
articles.summary: Ilhan Omar’s husband, political consultant Tim Mynett, has spoken out after federal agents raided the Minnesota congresswoman’s Washington, DC, residence
articles.body: Ilhan Omar’s husband, political consultant Tim Mynett, has spoken out after federal agents raided the Minnesota congresswoman’s Washington, DC, residence as part of a criminal investigation into her immigration records, while also addressing questions about her reported absence from public view.Mynett was seen leaving the couple’s rented home on Wednesday to walk their golden Labrador, Teddy, and later to take out the trash, according to the New York Post. He was also seen accompanying one of Omar’s staffers out of the house.Asked by Fox News Digital whether Omar had left the country amid rumours following the raid, Mynett expressed frustration with reporters and said their presence was disturbing neighbours.“You guys are annoying the hell out of all the neighbors around here, man,” he said.The developments come amid an investigation by Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) into Omar’s immigration paperwork. Federal agents searched her home on Monday, reportedly seizing her cellphone and passport, along with other items, according to US media reports.The investigation is examining questions surrounding Omar’s age at the time her family arrived in the US and the circumstances under which she obtained citizenship. The precise scope of the criminal investigation has not been publicly established.Mynett has maintained that he has no concerns about the investigation. Speaking to Fox News Digital earlier this week, he said Omar came to the US as a child refugee.“My wife came here when she was 12 years old as a child war refugee,” Mynett said. “No concerns.”Omar's relatives reportedly subpoenaedThe investigation has also reportedly extended to Omar’s relatives, with at least two family members receiving subpoenas, according to Fox News Digital. One of them was identified in reports as her sister, Sahra Noor.Omar, who was born in Somalia, arrived in the US in 1995 with her family after fleeing the country’s conflict. She became a naturalised US citizen in 2000.Questions have been raised about whether her age was accurately recorded in immigration documents. Reports have also highlighted a change to her birth year in records maintained by the Minnesota Legislative Reference Library, from 1981 to 1982.The allegations have drawn renewed scrutiny from Republicans, including President Donald Trump, who has previously questioned Omar’s citizenship and accused her of wrongdoing. Omar has rejected the allegations and described the investigations as politically motivated.Financial disclosures under scrutinySeparately, US Attorney Jeanine Pirro has confirmed that her office is investigating Omar’s financial disclosures, adding another dimension to the scrutiny surrounding the congresswoman.The issue gained attention after Omar’s 2024 congressional financial disclosure listed business interests associated with Mynett, including a winery and a venture capital advisory firm, with a combined reported value running into millions of dollars.Omar’s office subsequently amended the filing, saying the original disclosure had mistakenly reflected the total equity of the businesses rather than Mynett’s individual ownership interests. It also said the initial figures did not account for liabilities.In the amended records, Mynett’s ownership interests in both businesses were listed at zero dollars, according to reports.Trump questioned the discrepancy in a social media post on Tuesday, asking how Omar’s reported net worth could have reached as high as USD 30 million before being revised substantially downward.Officials have indicated that the inquiry into Omar’s financial disclosures is separate from the search of her residence. Omar has denied wrongdoing in connection with the allegations.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Oh(io) No: Hindu American Vivek Ramaswamy's Catch-22 problem with MAGA ahead of the midterms
articles.summary: Vivek Ramaswamy faces a unique challenge in Ohio's political landscape, caught between Trumpism's loyalty and the need to appeal to moderates. As he navigates his identity and support base ahead of the midterms, the impacts of MAGA's diminishing approval ratings loom large over his gubernatorial aspirations.
articles.body: The Indian identity has always cast a strange shadow over America, even before the USA came into existence. Christopher Columbus – who never reached the present-day mainland US and yet became one of its founding symbols because Americans needed something to differentiate themselves from the British, and an Italian voyager flying under the Spanish flag made for better storytelling – called the natives “Indians”.The name came from Columbus believing that the Antilles were part of the Asian lands Europeans called the Indies, and Native Americans got stuck with the “Indian” label for centuries because, when a European makes a mistake, our colonial legacy ensures it lives on almost infinitely.Indians would arrive later in the US of A to provide various services, what comedian Nimesh Patel labels “gas, beds, and meds”, but today the Indian identity on the right side of American politics is going through what can be called a sticky wicket.On one side, you have Indian boy Kash Patel living the high life (his critics will argue literally) as the head of the FBI, flying around to chug beer with hockey teams when he’s not bragging about his country-singer girlfriend. On another, you have avowed Trump fan Dinesh D’Souza, who recently lost his cool on Twitter against racist Americans whom he perhaps considered his bedfellows.When someone mocked Vivek Ramaswamy’s failed attempts at carrying a child and wrote, “In case you’re wondering how England was able to take over the subcontinent of India with like a platoon of guys”, D’Souza hit back: “Yeah but one half-naked Indian guy was able to chase the British out in 1947 without firing a single shot.”It’s a peculiar stage where a man who has spent his life currying favour with white racists suddenly invokes Mahatma Gandhi in an argument against them. And perhaps the man who truly epitomises this dichotomy in the Indian-American identity is Vivek Ramaswamy.As The Economist noted, Vivek Ramaswamy has the odd problem of being “too MAGA and not MAGA enough”. The piece states: “…most polls show Dr Acton with a slight lead. Mr Ramaswamy is proving too MAGA for Ohio’s moderates and not MAGA enough for many Republicans.”He is running to become Ohio governor, a position he perhaps sees as a stepping stone to something bigger in the party. Yet Ramaswamy’s association with Trump is increasingly becoming a liability among neutral voters, while his faith and skin colour are proving a deterrent among parts of the MAGA base.He had many of the talking points of Trumpism with smoother syntax, fewer digressions and the confidence of a man who had sold his pharma company for hundreds of millions. And it was apparent that he understood MAGA’s most abiding philosophy: Trump is God and all else is embellishment.This was how Ramaswamy tamed anti-Indian MAGA by winning the Republican primary at a canter after Trump’s endorsement, but the upcoming midterms involve people who never agreed to that arrangement.The MAGA flag is flying at an all-time low – much of it thanks to Trump’s actions that have thrown the global economy into disarray – and hitting voters where it matters the most: their wallets.CNN’s October poll puts Amy Acton at 50% and Vivek at 42% among likely voters. Trump, who carried Ohio by 11 points in 2024, had an approval rating of 36% in the state. One poll doesn’t make a summer, but it does show that the presidential blessing now comes with significantly more baggage. It turns out war – that leads to global upheavals – isn’t great for the economy, at least not the way it used to be during World War II. The globe is just too interconnected now.His opponent, Acton, makes an awkward villain. She led Ohio’s pandemic response under Republican governor Mike DeWine, and while Trump calls her a “radical left-lunatic”, voters remember her as someone who has been associated with the state’s existing administration.The blast radius of Trump’s actions – MAGA lives and dies with his actions – isn’t just confined to Vivek.Pew’s late-September and early-October survey put Trump’s national approval at 30%. Even among his 2024 voters, approval has fallen from 95% to 67%. Ramaswamy’s short political career has always been the afterglow of Trump’s solar power, but now he has to negotiate an electorate that has got sunburnt.Joseph Heller, the author of Catch-22, would have found the contradiction quite amusing. Ramaswamy needs Trump to keep the MAGA base and needs to demonstrate to neutral voters that he’s not Trump.The problem here is balancing Otto von Bismarck’s art of the possible and improbable. The problem is that no matter what Vivek does, even if he balances a Bible on his head while reciting the Constitution, he would be judged for his skin colour and religion. Even if he converted like Bobby Jindal or Nikki Haley, or were a born Christian like Dinesh D’Souza, he would still be castigated for not being white. Racism simply never ends.The more sophisticated version of this prejudice now travels under the label of the heritage American, which sounds like a protected variety of cheese but essentially means that some Americans are more American than others because their ancestors arrived earlier. The exact date of arrival also varies. Some believe anyone who didn’t come on the Mayflower doesn’t qualify to be a heritage American. Others go back a few centuries. Sometimes, it’s just white immigrants.Ramaswamy’s political identity is based on the Reaganesque idea that “anyone, from any corner of the Earth, can come to live in America and become an American.”And now Reagan’s party – cannibalised by MAGA – no longer believes that. Of course, Ramaswamy has a style of conscientious arrogance that is great for start-up bros but isn’t particularly helpful for politicians not named Donald. Even Obama was accused of being a tad harrowing, so it’s hardly a surprise that Ramaswamy’s Boxing Day lecture about “American mediocrity”, asking Americans to watch less television and study more, sounded like something a Tiger Mom would tell her immigrant children.After all, the movement’s enthusiasm for colourless merit hit a snag when it appeared that Indians were winning it. Even Malcolm Gladwell has noted that America’s current positive affirmation movement hits Indian-Americans the hardest, which is starting to manifest as resentment against Indians.Consider the viral photo of Indian-American students attending a University of Texas football game where they were somehow targeted for doing the most American thing ever: drinking beer from a Viking horn while cheering on a football team. This was presented by Bo French, the Republican candidate for Texas Railroad Commissioner, as evidence of something wrong with the country.It’s remarkable because the same crowd, if they saw Indian-Americans watching cricket, would argue that immigrants are not assimilating enough. And when they do assimilate, it’s passed off as an invasion.Even MAGA’s colourless merit argument hits a snag with brown-skinned Indians. As Jonathan Chait documented in The Atlantic, Christopher Rufo, the conservative activist best known for campaigning against critical race theory, and right-wing publisher Jonathan Keeperman discussed the matter in a podcast ominously titled “The Indian Question”. Rufo complained about Indians spending endless hours preparing for spelling bees. Keeperman preferred the football player who spent the night drinking beer and still scored 1500 on his SATs.Ergo, we hit the heritage American qualification, but the fallout of anti-India and anti-Hindu hate – that used to be the preserve of America’s Left – now has bipartisan appeal.The online hatred exploded into the real world, like in the recent case of a 19-year-old who was arrested after an alleged mass-shooting plot targeting a Hindu place of worship in Aurora. Ironically, Ramaswamy, who has been very vocal about being Hindu, hasn’t weighed in on the attack, even though various Hindu American politicians like Ro Khanna and Suhas Subramanyam have condemned it, as have Republican ones like Rick McCormick and Darin LaHood.But Ramaswamy – at least at the time of writing – doesn’t appear to have used any press conference or social media account or given a word through his campaign. Which is a bit ironic, given that the proverbial cat has got the tongue of one of the nation’s most prominent Hindu Americans – who is wont to weigh in on every topic.Also read: How Vivek Ramaswamy tamed 'anti-Indian' MAGA and Donald TrumpMake America Smart Again? Donald Trump channels Vivek Ramaswamy and torpedoes MAGA's anti-immigrant rhetoricHow anti-India hate went mainstream in America, offline and online2025: The year America normalised anti-India hateMAGA's Carthage Moment? Why Donald Trump's empire might crumble because of decay withinIt’s perhaps just a continuation of his Catch-22 problem: ahead of the midterms, Ramaswamy doesn’t want to aggravate any potential voter already on the fence between Trump’s misadventures and his Hindu identity. Or perhaps he’s just waiting for Trump to weigh in.But if Ramaswamy does manage to win despite being caught between a rock and a hard place, it would be quite remarkable. Though perhaps not as remarkable as a country that spent centuries celebrating a man who never actually found it.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: A 19-year-old neo-Nazi teen’s reported use of cross-sex hormones has added a contentious dimension to an attempted mass
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: A 19-year-old neo-Nazi teen’s reported use of cross-sex hormones has added a contentious dimension to an attempted mass shooting at a Hindu temple in Illinois, while in a separate incident, a 16-year-old with access to guns murdered three children and a teacher in a school in Oregon as America’s epidemic of gun violence continues unabated.US politicians and public officials issued familiar mealy-mouthed platitudes invoking “thoughts and prayers” for victims and their families as the core issue of easy access to guns was sidelined by fervent debates over parenting, mental illness, gender transition, etc.Reports that Alexandro Paporakis, the Illinois gunman whose jammed rifle thwarted a carnage at a Hindu temple near Chicago and who was receiving cross-sex hormone therapy and that a judge had ordered treatment to continue in custody was the digression US gun enthusiasts leaned into to argue guns are not the problem.Court reporting also cited anxiety, depression and other medical treatment the teen was going through, although these issues and reported gender transition were not seen as evidence of a motive, at least initially, for the alleged attack.Investigators have pointed instead to white-supremacist ideology and explicit racial motive based on a manifesto expressing hatred toward Indians, Jews and Black people.The Illinois case has also acquired a personal dimension for local Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi, who said he and his family were present when the alleged attack was attempted Sunday.“I am horrified that a white supremacist attempted to carry out a mass shooting targeting Indian Americans at the Hindu temple in Aurora where my family worships,” the Illinois Democrat said, warning that anti-Indian hatred and white supremacy had become dangerous and authorities must take threats seriously before innocent people are killed.Six Indian-origin lawmakers – all Democrats – dubbed the “Samosa caucus” have faced virulent attacks from the MAGA nativist hardliners, some of them demanding only those born in the USA should be allowed to run for office.Among those who have faced such hostile race-baiting is Washington Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal, who has also faced attacks from many Indians for framing the Illinois incident more broadly in terms of attacks on South Asians, rather than explicitly describing the target as a Hindu temple, as her own party leader, New York Senator Chuck Schumer, did.Critics argue that describing a specifically anti-Hindu attack as anti-South Asian risks obscuring the religious identity of the intended victims.“Look at the chicanery of this lady. The word “ Hindu” gets stuck in her throat. Attacks by white supremacists are against Hindus, not “South Asians”. The targeted temple is Hindu, not South Asian. articles.title: In 2001, Ben Chestnut and Dan Kurzius built Mailchimp as a side project inside their Atlanta web-design agency and took no outside funding; 20 years later Intuit acquired the company for about $12 billion
articles.summary: Mailchimp began not as a billion-dollar startup with venture backing, but as a practical tool created inside a struggling Atlanta web-design agency.
articles.body: Mailchimp began not as a billion-dollar startup with venture backing, but as a practical tool created inside a struggling Atlanta web-design agency. In 2001, Ben Chestnut and Dan Kurzius built the email-marketing service to help small-business clients stay in touch with their customers. Twenty years later, that side project had become one of the most recognisable software brands in the world and was acquired by Intuit for approximately $12 billion.The story is especially striking because Mailchimp remained privately held for its entire life before the acquisition. According to Mailchimp’s own founder page, the company was co-founded by Chestnut and Kurzius in 2001 and had more than 1,500 employees and 13 million global users by the time Intuit bought it in 2021. Intuit’s SEC filing confirms that the deal closed on November 1, 2021, with total consideration of about $12 billion, made up of roughly $5.7 billion in cash and 10,090,414 Intuit shares.It started as a survival toolChestnut and Kurzius were not trying to build a global marketing platform when they created Mailchimp. They ran a web-design agency called The Rocket Science Group, and their clients were mostly small businesses that needed affordable ways to communicate with customers. Email marketing became the answer to a real operational problem rather than a product born from a pitch deck.The founders’ backgrounds shaped the company’s culture. Chestnut studied industrial design at Georgia Tech and later served as Mailchimp’s chief executive for more than two decades. Kurzius was a developer who also became the company’s first support agent, helping shape a customer-first approach that remained central to Mailchimp’s identity.That early connection to small businesses mattered. Mailchimp was not designed primarily for large corporations with big marketing departments. It was built for people who needed a straightforward way to send newsletters, promote products and build relationships with customers without hiring an expensive agency.No outside funding, no conventional pathMailchimp’s growth story stands apart from the familiar startup playbook. Many technology companies raise venture capital early, spend aggressively to capture market share and pursue rapid expansion. Mailchimp took a different route, remaining privately held until its acquisition in 2021.That independence gave the founders room to build at their own pace. Instead of chasing investor expectations, they could focus on making the product useful, keeping customers satisfied and growing the business sustainably. The company’s later scale suggests that this approach worked: by the time of the acquisition, Mailchimp had become a leading email and automation platform for growing businesses.The acquisition also showed how valuable a profitable, customer-focused software business can become. Intuit described Mailchimp as a global customer engagement and marketing platform for small and mid-market businesses, a description that reflects how far the company had moved beyond its origins as a simple email tool.Why Intuit wanted MailchimpIntuit did not acquire Mailchimp simply because it was a successful email company. The acquisition fit a broader strategy to create an end-to-end customer growth platform for small and mid-market businesses. Intuit already owned products such as QuickBooks, TurboTax, Mint and Credit Karma, giving it a large base of customers who managed money, taxes and business operations through its tools.Mailchimp added a missing piece: helping those businesses find, reach and retain customers. Intuit said the combined company would offer an AI-driven platform to help small and mid-market businesses prosper, connecting financial tools with marketing and customer engagement.The deal’s structure also reflected Mailchimp’s scale. Intuit paid approximately $5.7 billion in cash and issued more than 10 million shares of its common stock, according to its regulatory filing. The filing further noted that Intuit incurred $4.7 billion in term-loan debt in connection with the acquisition.The brand became part of the productMailchimp’s success was not only technical. Its quirky name, playful monkey mascot and distinctive design helped it stand out in a crowded software market. At a time when many business tools felt formal and impersonal, Mailchimp made email marketing feel approachable for people who had never run a digital campaign before.That personality became a competitive advantage. Small-business owners did not just use Mailchimp; they recognised it. The brand’s accessibility helped it grow from an internal agency project into a platform used by millions of businesses around the world.The company’s reputation also extended beyond its product. Mailchimp was named Inc. Magazine’s 2017 Company of the Year, recognised by Fast Company as one of the world’s most innovative companies and a Brand That Matters, and appeared on the Forbes Cloud 100 for six consecutive years.What founders can learn from MailchimpMailchimp’s journey offers a useful lesson for entrepreneurs: a business does not need to begin with a grand vision to become significant. Chestnut and Kurzius started by solving a practical problem for their agency’s clients, then kept improving the product as customer needs evolved.Their decision to avoid outside funding was not a guarantee of success, but it allowed them to retain control and build patiently. By the time Intuit acquired Mailchimp, the company had grown into a business with global reach, thousands of employees and a valuation of roughly $12 billion.The Mailchimp story shows that lasting companies often come from close attention to customers, not from chasing trends. A side project built to help small businesses send emails became a major force in digital marketing because its founders understood the people they were serving and gave themselves two decades to get it right.You use AI every day. articles.title: Hexagon World Series mira a 2027 desde Abu Dhabi
articles.standfirst: La competición internacional por equipos reunirá los días 21 y 22 de octubre a jugadores, equipos, representantes de la FIP y medios de comunicación en el Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental
articles.summary: La competición internacional por equipos reunirá los días 21 y 22 de octubre a jugadores, equipos, representantes de la FIP y medios de comunicación en el Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental
articles.body: Abu Dhabi será el escenario elegido por Hexagon World Series para avanzar algunos de los detalles más importantes de su proyecto de cara a 2027. La organización celebrará los próximos 21 y 22 de octubre de 2026 un evento exclusivo en el Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental, en el que se darán a conocer novedades y próximos pasos de la competición antes de su primera temporada completa. La cita congregará a una amplia representación del mundo del pádel, con la participación de miembros de Hexagon World Series, representantes de la Federación Internacional de Pádel (FIP), equipos y jugadores. A ellos se sumarán medios de comunicación internacionales y regionales, además de distintos invitados vinculados a la industria deportiva. Uno de los momentos principales del encuentro será la rueda de prensa, en la que la organización explicará la evolución del proyecto y ofrecerá nuevos detalles sobre los planes diseñados para la temporada 2027. El programa también incluirá varios anuncios relacionados con el futuro inmediato de la competición. La presencia de periodistas permitirá, además, establecer contacto directo con responsables de Hexagon World Series, representantes de la FIP y algunos de los jugadores que formarán parte del proyecto, facilitando entrevistas y encuentros con sus principales protagonistas. La reunión de Abu Dhabi llega en una fase decisiva para Hexagon World Series, que ultima la puesta en marcha de su primera temporada completa. El calendario ya cuenta con una primera gran cita confirmada: la GENERALI Hexagon Cup Madrid, que se disputará del 21 al 24 de enero de 2027 en la Caja Mágica y dará el pistoletazo de salida a la nueva temporada. El Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental, ubicado frente al mar en Abu Dhabi, será el punto de encuentro para esta presentación internacional. El reconocido hotel de lujo destaca tanto por su arquitectura como por su oferta gastronómica y se ha convertido en escenario habitual de grandes acontecimientos internacionales. A lo largo de los años, sus instalaciones han acogido eventos de muy distinta naturaleza, desde estrenos de cine y actuaciones musicales hasta importantes reuniones empresariales. En esta ocasión, el emblemático recinto servirá como punto de partida para conocer las novedades con las que Hexagon World Series afrontará su llegada a 2027.

articles.title: Meet Mike Satterlee, 19, who turned a $500 3D printer into a 160-printer New York operation after CruiseCup generated $808,000 in gross revenue in 2025
articles.summary: At 19, Mike Satterlee has already learned one of the more unpredictable rules of modern entrepreneurship: a single social media post can change the scale
articles.body: At 19, Mike Satterlee has already learned one of the more unpredictable rules of modern entrepreneurship: a single social media post can change the scale of a business almost overnight. What began with a $500 3D printer in his parents’ basement has grown into a New York operation running 160 printers and producing thousands of drink accessories, with CruiseCup generating $808,000 in gross revenue in 2025, states an online report by Traders Union.From a $500 printer to a businessAccording to CNBC report, Satterlee first encountered 3D printing during a high school design and production class. In September 2022, he used savings from birthdays, Christmas and earlier business ventures to buy his first printer for around $500. His first serious 3D-printing venture was Solefully, a business producing shoe charms for Crocs. Started in his parents’ basement in June 2023, it eventually generated about $250,000 in sales during 2024, giving the teenager enough traction to take the operation beyond the family home, the report adds.By November 2024, he was renting a 3,000-square-foot warehouse in Clifton Park, New York, for $3,600 a month. The space would eventually become the base for a much larger printing operation.Finding a better productAs Satterlee experimented with new ideas, he noticed that products designed around everyday problems attracted more attention online. Universal car cupholder adapters, capable of holding everything from coffee cups to large reusable bottles, performed better on social media and offered stronger margins than the shoe charms, states the Traders Union report.That discovery eventually led to CruiseCup. In June 2025, Satterlee shut down Solefully and focused entirely on the new business, adds the report. And the turning point came two months later when he designed a hard-shell insulated cooler capable of holding two 12-ounce cans. Unlike conventional double-can holders, the design could be loaded from either the top or bottom, the report elaborates.When social media changed everythingSatterlee promoted the new product through Instagram, where the design quickly gained attention. Orders surged into the hundreds in a single day, leaving his 60 printers facing a backlog that could have taken roughly six weeks to clear. Also, instead of turning customers away, Satterlee waited for the incoming revenue to finance additional equipment. CruiseCup generated about $100,000 in August alone, its strongest month at that point.The momentum continued and across its website and TikTok Shop, CruiseCup generated $808,000 in gross revenue during 2025, with a small additional amount coming from Amazon, Traders Union report adds.Reinvesting instead of cashing outAlthough the company is profitable, Satterlee is not treating the revenue as personal income. Living with his parents means he does not currently have rent expenses, allowing him to put most of the money back into the business. He typically takes between $500 and $1,500 a month for himself, while the remainder goes toward new printers, advertising and product development. The company is operated full-time by Satterlee and one other employee. The operation has now expanded to 160 printers, producing plastic products in New York. CruiseCup also sources stainless-steel versions from a manufacturer in China, the report adds.Building beyond the viral momentThe challenge for Satterlee now is turning a successful product into a lasting brand. He has two patents pending for CruiseCup designs and plans to introduce UV printing, expand its drinkware range and strengthen the company's marketing operation. He also hopes to move beyond direct online sales and eventually place CruiseCup products on retail shelves, concludes the CNBC report.Images Courtesy: Entrepreneur and istockYou use AI every day. articles.title: A 500-year-old Suffolk pub was partly destroyed by fire in 2013; 450 community shareholders helped raise over £400,000 to bring it back
articles.summary: Few things matter more to a village than its pub.
articles.body: Few things matter more to a village than its pub. In Wickham Market, East Suffolk, that truth was tested when fire partially destroyed The George, a building thought to be 500 years old, in 2013. Instead of watching it disappear, local people stepped forward. Hundreds became shareholders, volunteers gave thousands of hours, and a decade of determined fundraising followed. Today the Grade II listed pub is open again, serving as a meeting place and a home for community activities. Read on to discover how one village turned a devastating fire into a lasting example of community ownership and heritage conservation.The George in Wickham Market, a Grade II listed pub, thought to be 500 years old, was hit by fire in 2013The George is a Grade II listed pub in Wickham Market, a historic market village in East Suffolk. According to the National Lottery Heritage Fund, which published the story on its website, the building is thought to be 500 years old and sits within the village's conservation area, a designation that recognises the special architectural and historic character of a place. In 2013, fire partially destroyed the pub. For many villages, a loss like that would have meant the end of a beloved local gathering place. Instead, local people formed a community benefit society, an organisation run for the good of the wider community, with a clear goal, buy the building, restore it, and run it as a community pub and social enterprise.How 450 community shareholders contributed more than £400,000 over ten years to save their village pubWhat happened next is a lesson in patience. The National Lottery Heritage Fund reports that the local group spent ten years fundraising to bring The George back. During that decade, 450 community shareholders contributed, and together they put in more than £400,000. A community shareholding model like this gives ordinary residents a direct stake in a local asset, turning customers and neighbours into part-owners with a say in its future. It also demonstrates how many people were prepared to back a pub that many might have considered lost. Colin Owens, project lead of the venue's management committee, told the National Lottery Heritage Fund that the volunteer group raised in excess of £2 million overall to complete the project, a total well above the shareholders' contribution alone.National Lottery Heritage Fund grants worth £1.8 million helped rescue Wickham Market's last pubCommunity money was only part of the picture. The National Lottery Heritage Fund, the organisation behind the project page this article draws on, awarded £1.8 million in Heritage Enterprise grants to help rescue Wickham Market's last pub. Its project data lists the applicant as The George Community Pub (Wickham Market) Limited and records an award of £1,815,424, made on 3 September 2019. That support arrived years after the fire and during the decade of fundraising. Combined with the shareholders' investment, it gave the group the financial footing to proceed with restoration. For anyone studying how to save a threatened local landmark, the lesson is clear: community commitment and National Lottery heritage funding can work together to achieve what neither could manage alone.Restoring The George: ten thousand volunteer hours, hidden historic features, and a modern extensionThe restoration was a major undertaking. The National Lottery Heritage Fund says the project's volunteers estimate they spent 10,000 hours seeing the work through to completion. Spread across a standard full-time working year of about 2,000 hours, that equals roughly five years of work. Along the way, they uncovered and restored the building's historic features, including wooden beams and bricked-up staircases. A new extension adapted the pub for modern commercial use and added a kitchen and an accessible toilet, while a new lift now serves the first-floor community space. The volunteers also researched the pub's past, tracing landlords back to 1746, and used their findings in displays inside the building. The result blends old and new, a centuries-old structure with its character revealed, and the practical facilities a busy twenty-first-century venue requires.A reopened village hub since 2025, new jobs, a community choir, a wellbeing café, and award recognitionThe George reopened in September 2025, with a ribbon-cutting on 4 September. According to the National Lottery Heritage Fund, the reopening created several new jobs in a rural village. The first-floor community space now hosts weekly activities, including a wellbeing café, exercise classes, and a community choir. Recognition followed quickly, in 2025, the team won a Rural Community Business Award and was joint runner-up in the Campaign for Real Ale's Pub Saving Awards. Colin Owens told the National Lottery Heritage Fund that the volunteers wanted to restore the pub "to be more than a pub." Judging by the weekly activities, jobs, and awards, that ambition appears to be coming true, and The George now stands as an encouraging example for other communities facing the loss of a local landmark.You use AI every day. articles.title: Drake approached over George Foreman’s $6 million Texas mansion with 12,000-sq-ft home, 50-car garage and iconic grill kitchen; rapper already owns a $15 million ranch spanning 313 acres
articles.summary: Could Drake be the next owner of George Foreman’s spectacular Texas mansion?
articles.body: Could Drake be the next owner of George Foreman’s spectacular Texas mansion? The property, once home to the legendary heavyweight boxer and entrepreneur, is now on the market for $6 million, offering a rare combination of celebrity history, luxury living and an extraordinary car collection space.According to a report by the Daily Mail, Evan Compean, founder of the Compean Group, which is handling the listing, has already contacted representatives for Drake to explore whether the Canadian rapper might be interested in the property. The approach comes as the Grammy-winning superstar already owns a sprawling Texas ranch roughly an hour away.There is, however, no indication that Drake has expressed an intention to purchase the mansion. For now, the possibility offers an intriguing glimpse into the real estate choices available to celebrities seeking privacy, space and distinctive properties.Inside George Foreman’s $6 million Texas mansionLocated in Huffman, northeast of Houston, the Mediterranean-style estate was the longtime family home of Foreman, who died in March 2025 at the age of 76.Built in 2001, the property sits on 13.49 acres behind a gated entrance. Foreman and his wife, Mary Joan Martelly, designed the residence after their family outgrew their previous home in nearby Kingwood.Spanning nearly 12,000 square feet, the single-storey mansion has five bedrooms, nine bathrooms, two kitchens, multiple living rooms, a library, two offices and a fitness room. The interiors feature imported marble, hardwood flooring, elaborate woodwork, decorative columns and three fireplaces.One of its most striking features is a dramatic glass atrium at the centre of the house. With steel framing and a soaring glass ceiling, the space allows natural light to flood the entrance while separating the home's two wings.The property also has a particularly personal touch: a hair salon that Foreman reportedly built for his wife.The iconic kitchen where George Foreman filmed grill commercialsBeyond its size and luxury amenities, the mansion carries a piece of commercial history associated with one of Foreman’s most successful ventures.The kitchen where he filmed advertisements for the George Foreman Grill remains part of the property. Its island bears his initials, preserving a reminder of the business that helped transform the former heavyweight champion into a household name beyond boxing.Foreman won Olympic gold in 1968 and became world heavyweight champion in 1973. After stepping away from the sport, he made a remarkable comeback, knocking out Michael Moorer in 1994 at the age of 45 to become the oldest world heavyweight champion at the time.Yet his commercial success extended far beyond the boxing ring. The George Foreman Grill became a major hit, selling millions of units and establishing him as one of the most recognisable personalities in consumer advertising.The kitchen is therefore more than another feature in an expensive home. It is a tangible connection to the second chapter of Foreman’s extraordinary career.An 11,000-square-foot garage that can house more than 50 carsFor automobile enthusiasts, the mansion’s biggest attraction could be the enormous collector’s garage behind the main residence.Measuring approximately 11,000 square feet, the climate-controlled facility was designed to accommodate a substantial collection of vehicles. The space could potentially serve as a private car museum, although its next owner could also explore alternative uses.According to the listing, the garage could be converted into a boxing gym, basketball court or another recreational facility.Foreman had a well-documented passion for cars and owned dozens of vehicles. He eventually sold more than 50 cars at auction, and the garage is now empty, ready for a new owner to decide how to use the space.For someone with Drake’s financial resources and interest in large, private properties, the facility could be an appealing feature. However, there is no confirmation that the rapper has visited the estate or considered purchasing it.George Foreman’s estate offers additional land, tennis and basketball courtsThe 13.49 acres currently being offered for sale form part of a larger estate measuring approximately 28 acres.A further 14.79-acre parcel is available separately, potentially allowing a buyer to expand the property into an even larger private compound.The additional land includes a tennis court, basketball court and fishing pond, creating opportunities for outdoor recreation away from the main residence.The estate also has a private well, septic system and whole-home generator, features that support a more self-contained lifestyle.Situated in Huffman, the property offers a rural atmosphere while remaining within reach of Houston. Lake Houston is nearby, adding to the appeal for buyers seeking a retreat without moving too far from a major city.George Foreman’s mansion was a family home, not just a luxury propertyWhile the estate boasts impressive dimensions and amenities, it also played an important role in Foreman’s family life.The mansion became a gathering place for his large family, with one of his daughters reportedly holding her wedding reception in the central glass atrium.Foreman also used the property as a base for his work outside boxing. A private studio and office provided space for his sermons as he pursued his career as a minister.He continued to make television appearances later in life, including on NBC’s travel reality series Better Late Than Never, alongside William Shatner, Henry Winkler and Terry Bradshaw.Now, more than a year after his death, the residence is seeking a new owner who could preserve its history or reshape it to suit a different lifestyle.Drake already owns a sprawling $15 million Texas ranchThe speculation surrounding Drake’s potential interest in Foreman’s former home stems partly from his existing Texas real estate holdings.The rapper reportedly paid around $15 million for the former Inn at Dos Brisas ranch near Chappell Hill. The property spans approximately 313 acres between Houston and Austin, giving him considerable space and privacy.His existing ranch has helped establish his presence in the Texas luxury property market, making the suggestion of another purchase an interesting possibility.Foreman’s former home would offer a different proposition. Although significantly smaller in acreage than Drake’s ranch, it combines a substantial residence, an exceptionally large garage, recreational possibilities and a direct connection to one of boxing’s most celebrated figures.The $6 million asking price is also considerably lower than the reported price of Drake’s existing ranch, though the two properties differ significantly in their size, features and potential uses.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision?
