articles.summary: An Indian-origin Metropolitan Police officer, Harman Singh, faces multiple charges including attempted rape and sexual assault in London. He is set to appear in court as allegations from January 2026 come to light. This incident follows a similar case involving another officer, Prakash Patel.
articles.body: An Indian-origin Metropolitan Police officer is due to appear before a London court after being charged with attempted rape, sexual assault and intentional strangulation over alleged offences against a woman earlier this year.Police Constable Harman Singh, attached to the force’s North Area command unit, faces five charges: one count of attempted rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of intentional strangulation. He is scheduled to appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on Monday, October 19, according to Metropolitan police.The allegations relate to an incident involving a woman in January 2026. The matter was reported to police that month, and Singh was arrested on January 10 on suspicion of attempted rape and two counts of sexual assault. He was subsequently released on bail pending further enquiries.Following an investigation by the Met Police, the case was referred to the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), which authorised the charges on September 4. Singh was suspended from duty after his arrest.Last month, another Indian-origin Metropolitan Police officer, Detective Sergeant Prakash Patel, was charged with five counts of sexual assault involving four women known to him. The allegations relate to incidents in summer 2024 and on December 3, 2024.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Israeli settlers attack Palestinian villages, torch cars and trees during olive harvest
articles.summary: Israeli settlers attacked at least eight Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank on Friday, setting cars and trees on fire and assaulting residents
articles.body: Israeli settlers attacked at least eight Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank on Friday, setting cars and trees on fire and assaulting residents and a foreign journalist, as violence disrupted the annual olive harvest.The attacks were reported by local officials and the Palestine Red Crescent Society in the northern West Bank, where much of the territory's olive production is concentrated. Tens of thousands of Palestinian families rely on the harvest for their livelihoods.The violence comes ahead of Israel's October 27 election, with settler attacks having risen sharply this year and intensified in recent weeks. The far-right government, accused of encouraging the settlers, faces the prospect of either losing power or securing another term.Rights groups slam Israeli forces Residents and human rights organisations say Israeli authorities have done little to stop settler attacks. They allege that soldiers have sometimes helped settlers, protected them or stood by while Palestinian villages came under assault.The violence has prompted accusations of “ethnic cleansing”, including from the British government, which accused Israel of turning a “blind eye” to the campaign.“Soldiers aren't stopping the violence or protecting Palestinians," said Ziv Stahl, executive director of Israeli rights group Yesh Din. “If anything, they're sometimes assisting settlers in the attacks.”The West Bank has been under Israeli military rule since the 1967 Middle East war. It is now home to around three million Palestinians and more than 500,000 Israeli settlers.The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs reported last month that more than 1,600 attacks had been recorded across the territory between January and August. Yesh Din and other rights groups say those responsible are rarely arrested or indicted.Disputed shooting in Abu FalahIn the village of Abu Falah, settlers attacked on Friday as residents, accompanied by peace activists, headed out early to harvest olives.Israeli troops later arrived and drove into the village after dispersing the crowd from the olive groves. Residents alleged that soldiers subsequently fired live ammunition at Abdel Jaber Hassan, a village council member, despite him being unarmed and away from the trees.The Israeli military said its soldiers had opened fire because an individual was running towards them carrying a sharp object. However, Nazem Saleh Shoman, another village council member, disputed that account, saying Hassan was shot at close range while carrying tools used for olive harvesting.The Israeli military condemned the violence on Friday and acknowledged that a journalist had been injured in Abu Falah.Dozens reported injured across the territoryThe attacks were not limited to Abu Falah. The Palestine Red Crescent Society said its medical teams had treated 14 injured people at six locations across the West Bank.Local officials reported at least four additional injuries in two other villages, bringing the reported number of injured people to at least 18 across the locations cited in the reports.The attacks have further disrupted the olive harvest, a crucial source of income for Palestinian families, amid growing concerns over settler violence and the ability of residents to access their farmland safely.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Chatribari Durga Puja Samiti in Guwahati to showcase a Rs 1.8 lakh Durga idol made from grains, pulses and spices alongside a clay idol.
articles.body: Guwahati: A Durga idol made entirely from grains, pulses and spices will be the main attraction at the Chatribari Durga Puja Samiti pandal this year.Crafted without soil by an artisan from Gossaigaon, the idol has cost around Rs 1.80 lakh. It uses paddy, rice, maize, mustard seeds, red lentils, green gram, peas, kidney beans, peanuts, cardamom, cinnamon, dried chillies and betel nuts.“The committee will install two idols at the pandal this year, one traditional clay idol and the other made entirely from these food items. Artists have been involved in crafting both idols, with the unusual creation expected to be one of the main attractions for visitors,” said Babul Rajbongshi, cultural secretary of the puja committee.The committee will install both the food-based idol and a traditional clay idol at the pandal. articles.title: Police intensify security for Dussehra and Navratri festivities
articles.summary: Prayagraj police tighten security for Navratri and Dussehra with patrols, traffic control, CCTV and drone surveillance at markets, pandals and Ramlila sites.
articles.body: Prayagraj: In view of the ongoing Ramlila and Durga Puja celebrations and the fast-approaching Dussehra festival, cops have significantly intensified patrolling and heightened security measures to ensure public safety. All prominent markets, ramlila sites and pandals have been taken under the police scanner. The festive fever has gripped the city during Navratri celebrations.With the volume of the crowd increasing at prominent markets and pandals to witness lighting during the ongoing Navratri celebrations, senior cops have deputed mobile squads at static locations. Besides, foot patrolling has also been intensified at all market spots, i.e., Civil Lines, to keep troublemakers at bay.A senior cop said, “In view of the massive footfall expected at festive venues, markets, and public places, cops are implementing multi-layered security protocols. A security plan has been drafted for Dussehra celebrations besides other key measures including foot and convoy patrolling.”Pointedly, senior police officials are actively leading extensive foot marches and convoy patrolling in crowded markets, narrow lanes, and sensitive residential zones. Specially constituted police teams are inspecting and elaborating security in and around ramlila grounds. articles.title: S Bengal got 8% more rain this monsoon, north 13% less
articles.summary: IMD report: South Bengal received 8% above-normal monsoon rain in 2026; Kolkata saw 28% surplus, while North Bengal recorded a 13% deficit.
articles.body: Kolkata: Powerful Bay systems, including depressions and low-pressure areas, kept the monsoon on track in Bengal in 2026. In Kolkata, the seasonal rain surplus was 28% and in South Bengal, the rain excess was 8%. North Bengal had a seasonal rain deficit of 13%. A deviation of plus or minus 15% is considered to be within normal range.In meteorological parameters, June-Sept is counted as the monsoon season. During this period, Kolkata recorded 1,718.9 mm rainfall against a normal of 1,345.5 mm. Overall, South Bengal logged 1,265.3 mm against the normal 1,166.8 mm. North Bengal recorded 1,647.1 mm against the normal value of 1,882.8 mm.Six monsoon depressions — two each in July, Aug and Sept — had formed over Bay of Bengal, with three intensifying into deep depressions. These systems ensured the monsoon current remained active on most days during the season.“Five out of these six depressions had an impact in the rain intensity and frequency in Bengal. Systems like these are important during the monsoon for sufficient rain,” said H R Biswas, head at Regional Meteorological Centre, Kolkata.Additionally, five low-pressure areas formed over north Bay of Bengal and adjoining coastal states — one in July, three in Aug and one in Sept. These, too, significantly influenced Bengal in terms of rain.According to a special monsoon report by IMD, the rain surplus was highest in East Midnapore at 48%, followed by West Midnapore at 40% and North 24 Parganas at 29%.“During monsoon, 101% of the long-period average (LPA) rainfall has occurred over Bengal,” the IMD special monsoon analysis report said.This year, the southwest monsoon arrived in North Bengal on June 9. It then advanced over most parts of South Bengal, including Kolkata, on June 12. By June 15, it had covered all of the state.The monsoon started retreating from parts of Bengal by Oct 12 and by Oct 15, it had departed from the state completely. Monsoon’s departure is considered normal when it happens between the first and second weeks of Oct.Despite Oct, Nov and Dec being known for cyclonic storms developing over Bay of Bengal, the Met office has ruled out any such system in the next two weeks.“We see no big system over Bay of Bengal in the next 10 days that could bring heavy rain,” added Biswas.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: 'American workers should come first in their own country': Republicans bring new bill to make H-1B visa salary threshold $140,000
articles.summary: At a time when Vice President JD Vance announced that he would like the H-1B visa program to be abolished, a few Republican leaders have proposed a new
articles.body: At a time when Vice President JD Vance announced that he would like the H-1B visa program to be abolished, a few Republican leaders have proposed a new legislation to increase the salary threshold of the H-1B visa holders so that there is no scope for American companies to hire foreign employees at a cheaper rate. Congressman Glenn Grothman (R-WI) introduced the Protecting American Workers Through H-1B Modernization Act, which would close an outdated loophole that allows H-1B dependent employers to bypass certain American worker protections. Senator Jon Husted (R-OH) has introduced companion legislation in the Senate.“American workers should come first in their own country,” said Grothman. “Employers should not be able to use a salary threshold established nearly three decades ago to bypass protections for qualified Americans. There is no excuse for leaving this threshold unchanged when it should have been raised years ago. Washington’s failure to act shows how little the Establishment cares about unemployed Americans when employers want access to cheap foreign labor. This bill would update that threshold and help ensure American workers have a fair opportunity to compete for these jobs.”“For decades, companies have been able to sidestep hiring American workers because of a salary threshold that hasn’t budged since 1998. That’s not modernization, that’s a loophole. This bill simply asks that when a company is heavily reliant on these visas and wants to bring in more H-1B workers, they shouldn’t be relying on an outdated law to get around offering these jobs to qualified American workers first,” said Husted.What is the present H-1B salary threshold? $60,000 per yearUnder current law, H-1B dependent employers, companies whose H-1B share of their workforce exceeds a particular threshold, must attest that they have first tried to hire American workers before sponsoring additional H-1B visas. However, employers are exempt if they pay the H-1B worker at least $60,000 per year, or if the worker holds a master’s degree or higher.The $60,000 threshold was set in 1998 and was intended to be twice the Social Security Administration’s (SSA) National Average Wage Index at the time. It has never been adjusted for inflation. Today, the SSA National Average Wage Index is nearly $70,000, meaning the original threshold, adjusted for inflation, would be nearly $140,000, the Republican leaders said.The Protecting American Workers Through H-1B Modernization Act would replace the fixed $60,000 threshold with a dynamic standard equal to two times the national average wage index, as calculated by the SSA. This would ensure the threshold keeps pace with wage growth going forward, rather than remaining frozen in place.It doesn't mean H-1Bs will get more salaryThe bill is just legislation and far from being approved. But even if it does, it won't make every H-1B earn $140,000 per year. it would raise the salary threshold at which a worker can qualify for the exemption which is now set at $60,000.You use AI every day. articles.title: Paediatrician saves flyer after suspected heart attack on Paris-Del flight
articles.summary: Paediatrician Prabir Bhaumik revived a 39-year-old passenger after suspected heart attack on Air India Paris–Delhi flight, stabilising him before Delhi landing.
articles.body: Kolkata: A paediatrician travelling from Paris to Kolkata via Delhi helped revive a critically ill passenger who collapsed midair on an overnight Air India flight. Prabir Bhaumik, who was on flight AI-142, had dozed off after the aircraft took off from Charles de Gaulle Airport at 8.45 pm local time on Wednesday. He woke up on hearing an emergency announcement asking if there was a doctor on board.Bhaumik responded and was taken to the rear galley, where he found a 39-year-old passenger lying on the floor while a crew member tried to administer oxygen.“The passenger’s oxygen saturation, heart rate and blood pressure were falling, and his pulse was weak. I suspected he suffered a myocardial infarction and began cardiopulmonary resuscitation. I instructed another person to use an Ambu bag mask,” the doctor told TOI on Friday.Bhaumik said he knew aspirin had to be administered, but it could be given only when the passenger was conscious. The passenger was given three doses of sorbitrate under his tongue at five-minute intervals while his blood pressure was monitored. “Samson, the patient, repeatedly regained consciousness and collapsed as his vital signs deteriorated. We had to monitor his condition every five minutes and resume CPR whenever his condition worsened. The captain repeatedly sought advice on whether an emergency landing was required. Thankfully, we managed to stabilise him after four hours,” Bhaumik said.Bhaumik handed the passenger over to a medical team when the flight landed in Delhi around 10 am on Thursday.“It was an experience I will never forget. I have encountered many emergencies involving children, but handling a critically ill adult 40,000 ft in the air with extremely limited medical support was a learning experience,” said Bhaumik, who owns a multispeciality paediatric hospital in Kolaghat.Bhaumik had travelled to Paris for the screening of ‘Pagla Ghoda’, a film he produced. Directed by Sekhar Das, the film is based on the eponymous play by theatre director Badal Sarkar.
